scenes.narration: Neuroscientists can detect a decision forming seconds before you are aware of having made one. Your conscious self is often the last to know.
In some studies, brain patterns predicted a button press up to ten seconds before the person reported deciding.
That ordering explains doubt. The choice is already running when your mind catches up and starts questioning it.
Under fatigue the automatic systems take over, which is why late night decisions repeat old patterns instead of breaking them.
The practical fix is to make big decisions in the morning, when the deliberate system still has fuel.
You are not slower than your brain. You are simply notified after the fact.
